newsitem.title: CANADA: Canada expected to approve Arctic diamond mine.
newsitem.headline: Canada expected to approve Arctic diamond mine.

text.p: Canada's federal government was expected to announce Friday final approval for an Arctic diamond mine proposed by Australia's Broken Hill Proprietary Co. Ltd. and Dia Met Minerals Ltd. of Canada.

Ron Irwin, the federal minister responsible for the North, other government officials and company representatives were due to attend a ceremony Friday morning in Yellowknife, capital of the Northwest Territories.
The companies are seeking to build a C$860 million ($647 million) diamond mine at Lac de Gras on the desolate Arctic frontier.

Investors have been eagerly awaiting a final decision after Canada gave approval in principle in August for the mine. It said then it hoped to grant final approval in early October and analysts said Thursday it was a virtual certainty that the final permission would be granted.
Government officials declined to comment on the nature of Friday's ceremony but sent strong signals that a positive decision would be announced.
"I can't really confirm that. All I can say is there will be a large event and an announcement will be made," a government spokeswoman said.
A spokeswoman for Dia Met said the companies had been invited by the federal government to a "protocol implementation ceremony."

Asked if this meant the government had granted its final approval, the Dia Met spokeswoman said, "It's very positive, that's what we're thinking." A BHP spokeswoman declined to comment but said an agenda for the event included the signing of a framework environmental agreement.

The government said previously it would grant final approval once BHP had made significant progress toward striking agreements on sharing economic benefits with local residents and environmental monitoring.
Since then BHP has been in intense negotiations and has sealed several accords. The environmental accord was one of the last hurdles to be overcome.
The companies want to begin construction immediately and hope to begin diamond mining in 1998. BHP has 51 percent of the project and Dia Met 29 percent.
The diamond mine would be Canada's first. BHP wants to take advantage of the winter to ship heavy construction materials to the remote site by a temporary road made of ice.
Dia Met stock was halted at midafternoon Thursday pending news. It last traded at C$20.25 ($15.23), down C25 cents (19 U.S. cents) in Toronto.
